Case Report
The patient is a 14-year-old girl with normal psychomotor development born to nonblood-related parents.

She started by presenting with focal seizures that were secondarily generalized and were treated by lamotrigine. These seizures were stereotypical and began with a sensation of nausea, disorientation and confusion, and chewing. After several weeks of progression and lamotrigine treatment, she gradually showed memory impairment with antegrade amnesia and recurrent episodes of loss of contact.
At 2 years of immunosuppressive treatment and rehabilitation, the course showed partial improvement of the memory and neuropsychiatric impairment, and epilepsy that continued to be active.
Three months after the start of care, the patient had painful lumbar stiffness with subacute onset and abdominal spasms.

extractions.quote: We began a treatment with sequential courses of intravenous corticosteroids (1 g per day for 5 days) and polyvalent immunoglobulins (1 g/kg/day for 2 days) every 3 weeks for 4 months. The antiepileptic treatment was replaced by zonisamide. She received care at the rehabilitation center between treatment courses and hospitalizations. After 3 months of treatment, there was mild improvement, but severe memory impairment and active signs of epilepsy continued. The GAD65 antibodies were still greater than 2000 IU/L in the serum and CSF. The MRI showed marked improvement in the inflammation signs but the start of atrophy of the amygdala. Due to these factors, a decision was made for a second line of treatment with rituximab (2 doses of 375 mg/m2) combined with two supplementary courses of corticosteroids and immunoglobulins. An overall follow-up assessment at 1 year of disease progression found epilepsy still active on zonisamide and oxcarbazepine, mild internal temporal atrophy on MRI (��Fig. 1. 2 ), and CSF still positive for antibodies, with high levels in the blood. The rituximab was continued every 6 months with a good CD19 and CD20 depletion, but also a decrease in gamma globulins necessitating supplementation. The latest year of follow-up showed no improvement on memory, an epilepsy stable with 1 crisis per months with sodium valproate and lacosamide, but recurrent psychotic episodes of 24 hours every 2 weeks and a progressive stiffness recurring. There was no decrease in the GAD65 antibodies in blood and CSF, and the MRI shows now a cortical and subcortical atrophy (��Fig. 1. 3 ). Recently, we decided to intensify the treatment with rituximab and cyclophosphamide.
